ds: Employers or labour providers underreport wages, create phantom workers, or operate short-lived 'ghost' companies that collect payroll funds and never remit social insurance or withholding tax. Common in labour-intensive sectors using subcontracting chains and agency labour.

src.t: OECD, Shining Light on the Shadow Economy: Opportunities and Threats (2017)
FATF/OECD, Money Laundering Awareness Handbook for Tax Examiners and Tax Auditors (2012)
ILO and tax authority guidance on undeclared work and bogus self-employment
FATF and OECD, Money Laundering Awareness Handbook for Tax Examiners and Tax Auditors (2012)

rat: Labour providers and ghost employers withdrawing cash payroll, paying workers via shared accounts, and bogus self-employment; employees are the payees.

ind.cx: Large cash withdrawals shortly after receiving client funds, close to total weekly wages, with no matching payroll tax payments.
ind.fp: Genuine cash-in-hand wages exist in some sectors.
ind.ds: Large cash withdrawals shortly after receiving client funds, close to total weekly wages, with no matching payroll tax payments.

ind.n: Short-lived labour supplier with rotating entities
ind.cx: Company wound up or abandoned within one to two years, with successor firm at same address, same workers and clients.
ind.fp: Contractors may restructure for commercial reasons.
ind.ds: Entities are repeatedly formed, abandoned or replaced by successors sharing directors, addresses or history of prior defaulted companies.
ind.cn: Short-lived or rotating entities with common controllers

ind.n: Workers paid to multiple accounts or via third parties
ind.cx: Salaries are paid into accounts that control multiple 'employees' or into one account for numerous workers.
ind.fp: Family or agency pooling can legitimately concentrate payments.
ind.ds: Wages are paid to accounts not held by the worker or split across several accounts.
ind.cn: Workers paid to third-party or multiple accounts

ind.n: Payroll volume inconsistent with declared headcount
ind.cx: Wages paid or invoiced greatly exceed declared staff and reported payroll tax. Labour provider shows no pension, insurance, equipment or accommodation costs.
ind.fp: Seasonal hires may inflate volumes. New firms may have lean cost bases.
ind.ds: Reported revenue, payroll or resident staff do not match the typical costs and workforce of the stated business model.
ind.cn: Business revenue inconsistent with staffing or operating costs

ind.n: Sole-trader or bogus self-employment structure for large workforce
ind.cx: Many workers treated as independent contractors despite working under direction for one client.
ind.fp: Contracting is lawful where genuinely independent.
ind.ds: Many workers treated as independent contractors despite working under direction for one client.

ind.n: Payments to workers just under tax or reporting thresholds
ind.cx: Pay split into amounts staying below withholding or reporting thresholds.
ind.fp: Part-time work may legitimately fall below thresholds.
ind.ds: Pay split into amounts staying below withholding or reporting thresholds.

ind.n: Multiple businesses sharing addresses, phones and bank signatories
ind.cx: A group of firms pooling workers share control and registered details with no group disclosed.
ind.fp: Business parks and accountants' addresses are shared.
ind.ds: Several apparently separate businesses or sub-accounts share owners, signatories, addresses, devices or bank accounts.

ctl.ds: Compares account flows with filed accounts, VAT or sales tax data and tax remittances, and links to VAT-fraud controls. It spots under-declared revenue and tax fraud proceeds.

ctl.n: Payroll and worker payment flow analytics
ctl.ds: Compares payroll flows with declared headcount, checks that wages reach workers' own accounts and flags cash payroll, recruiter payments and many-to-one wage patterns. It surfaces undeclared work and labour exploitation.

ctl.n: Labour provider and recruiter due diligence
ctl.ds: Verifies licences, ownership, registration, tax compliance and wage-payment evidence of labour providers and recruiters at onboarding and review, and checks recruitment practices. It reduces exposure to exploitative labour supply and undeclared work.

Links newly formed companies to failed or abandoned predecessors through shared officers, addresses, customers and bank details. It detects serial use of disposable entities to shed liabilities and move value.

ctl.n: Fan-in, fan-out and funnel account detection
ctl.ds: Detects accounts receiving from many unrelated senders, or sending to many beneficiaries, followed by consolidation or onward movement. It surfaces collector, funnel and mule structures.
Participates in sector, regulator and public-private forums and platform cooperation to receive and share typologies and indicators where lawful. It keeps scenarios current.

Compares actual activity with the customer's declared profile, history and peers and alerts on material or trend-breaking deviation, usually as a contextual signal. It catches change that rules on fixed thresholds miss.
Tailors training content and frequency to role and risk for finance, relationship, underwriting and compliance staff, with feedback of quality assurance findings. It builds baseline competence.
Detects repeated transactions placed just below reporting or approval limits, tuned by band and window per segment. It counters deliberate splitting designed to avoid scrutiny.

Requires a documented commercial or legal reason for each layer of a multi-tier or cross-border structure, with specialist review and sign-off before approval. Unexplained complexity is treated as a risk driver and can lead to decline.
Clusters customers, vendors and entities that share addresses, phones, devices, officers or bank details, including against staff records. It reveals common control and hidden relationships.
